title: PSG-SQLOG: square-root-log depth with a subquadratic-log copy exponent

claims.statement: For every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, with n=ceil(log2 N), the ONE PSG-SQLOG algorithm and exact integer parameter rule of proof.md recover the entire s from independent ideal copies with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8>2/3. On EVERY branch including all failed attempts, rejected or discarded copies, incorrect numerical-label branches, retries and both cutoff aborts, its total charged sequential work T is O(2^(n/(2*sqrt(log2 n))+6*n/(log2 n))). This full uniform bit-length envelope applies for n>=2; the explicit finite branch covers smaller n. Its exact envelope growth index is 1/1. All outer constants are absolute and independent of N,s and outcomes. This holds jointly with the other three resources and clean-only tolerance claim for the same algorithm/configuration.

For every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, with n=ceil(log2 N), the ONE PSG-SQLOG algorithm and exact integer parameter rule of proof.md recover the entire s from independent ideal copies with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8>2/3. On EVERY branch including all failed attempts, rejected or discarded copies, incorrect numerical-label branches, retries and both cutoff aborts, its peak classical bits S_C is O(n^2). This full uniform bit-length envelope applies for n>=2; the explicit finite branch covers smaller n. Its exact envelope growth index is 0/1. All outer constants are absolute and independent of N,s and outcomes. This holds jointly with the other three resources and clean-only tolerance claim for the same algorithm/configuration.

For every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, with n=ceil(log2 N), the ONE PSG-SQLOG algorithm and exact integer parameter rule of proof.md recover the entire s from independent ideal copies with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8>2/3. On EVERY branch including all failed attempts, rejected or discarded copies, incorrect numerical-label branches, retries and both cutoff aborts, its peak quantum wires S_Q is O(n). This full uniform bit-length envelope applies for n>=2; the explicit finite branch covers smaller n. Its exact envelope growth index is 0/1. All outer constants are absolute and independent of N,s and outcomes. This holds jointly with the other three resources and clean-only tolerance claim for the same algorithm/configuration.

For every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, with n=ceil(log2 N), the ONE PSG-SQLOG algorithm and exact integer parameter rule of proof.md recover the entire s from independent ideal copies with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8>2/3. On EVERY branch including all failed attempts, rejected or discarded copies, incorrect numerical-label branches, retries and both cutoff aborts, its total acquired source copies Q including all rejected and discarded copies is O(2^((log2 n)^(3/2))). This full uniform bit-length envelope applies for n>=2; the explicit finite branch covers smaller n. Its exact envelope growth index is 0/1. All outer constants are absolute and independent of N,s and outcomes. This holds jointly with the other three resources and clean-only tolerance claim for the same algorithm/configuration.

For the same PSG-SQLOG algorithm and complete parameter rule in proof.md, the proved malformed-sample fractional guarantee is epsilon(n)=0: all Q acquired source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N>=2 and every s, unconditional full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3 jointly with all four every-branch resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted, and this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
